adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:156 — Error timestamps from nodestore are in seconds while rrweb replay event timestamps are in milliseconds, so every error sorts before the first breadcrumb and the chronological interleaving silently does nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add interleaving logic that assumes `error_events[*]["timestamp"]` and replay segment `event["timestamp"]` are comparable, but the diff does not show that replay timestamps are milliseconds. In the added tests, replay event timestamps are floats like 1.5/2.0 and error timestamps are floats like 1.0/3.0 or `datetime.now().timestamp()` (seconds), implying consistent units in this PR’s context. There is no evidence in the diff that rrweb timestamps are in milliseconds while nodestore timestamps are in seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:100 — The full error_events list gets injected into every paginated page's Seer request no matter which segments are on that page, so errors are duplicated across pages and attributed to unrelated segments.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, `error_events` is fetched once from the replay instance (`fetch_error_details(...)`) and then passed into `paginate(..., on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events))`. Since `analyze_recording_segments` is invoked per paginated page (each page has a different `segments` list), every page’s Seer request calls `get_request_data(iter_segment_data(segments), error_events)` with the full replay-wide `error_events`. In `gen_request_data`, any errors with timestamps before/after the events in the current page are still emitted (before the first event, or after the last), so the same errors can be repeated across multiple pages and included alongside unrelated segment events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:107 — error_ids from the replay row are unbounded, so a replay with thousands of errors triggers an unbounded nodestore get_multi and an oversized Seer payload on each request.

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py the new logic pulls `error_ids` from the replay row (`error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", [])`) with no bounding/limiting, then calls `fetch_error_details(..., error_ids=error_ids)` which builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(...) for id in error_ids]` and performs an unbounded `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`. Those fetched errors are then merged into the `logs` list and JSON-encoded into the Seer request payload (`json.dumps({"logs": ...})`). A replay row containing thousands of `error_ids` will therefore trigger an unbounded nodestore read and can produce an oversized Seer payload per request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:115 — One report with an unknown/new type (strict ChoiceField) or bad field makes the whole batch return 422, dropping every valid report in it and making browsers retry the same poisoned batch.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, the code validates reports in a loop and immediately `return Response(..., status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(...)`). This rejects the entire batch even if earlier/later reports are valid, so one unknown `type` (ChoiceField) or other invalid field causes all valid reports in that request to be dropped/not processed, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:52 — The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness, so age=0 with a timestamp passes, and a report with neither field also passes validation.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Because these use truthiness, `age: 0` is treated as absent (falsey) and will not trigger the mutual-exclusion error even if `timestamp` is also present. Also, since both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False` and there is no object-level validation enforcing that at least one is provided, a report containing neither field will pass `is_valid()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:115 — This unauthenticated public endpoint logs the full raw_report at warning level and echoes validation details back, so an attacker can inflate logs with arbitrarily large payloads.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, the endpoint is unauthenticated (`permission_classes = ()`) and CSRF-exempt, and it logs untrusted payloads including the full request body at info (`logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})`) and, on invalid input, logs the full invalid data/report at warning (`browser_report_invalid_format` includes `data: raw_data`; `browser_report_validation_failed` includes `raw_report: report`). It also returns detailed validation errors to the caller (`Response({"error": ..., "details": serializer.errors}, 422)`), enabling log amplification and noisy/error-reflection behavior from an internet-facing endpoint when enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:37 — The owner ActorField accepts any user/team id without checking that the actor belongs to the detector's organization, so a detector can be assigned to a team or user from another org.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` and then simply copies the parsed actor IDs onto the `Detector` model in `create`/`update`, but the diff does not show `ActorField`’s implementation. Moreover, new tests were added that explicitly expect a 400 when the owner user is not in the organization (`tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py::test_owner_not_in_organization`), which strongly implies membership validation exists (likely inside `ActorField`). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:43 — New serializer requires `destination` and `attempts` (and `user_agent`) which Editor's Draft/Chrome report payloads (age,type,url,user_agent,body) do not send, so spec-compliant browser reports get 422 despite the "support both specs" comment

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:115 — A single invalid report now rejects the entire batch with 422 (and a JSON error body) instead of processing valid reports, changing endpoint status/response contract for browser clients

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the endpoint now validates each report with `BrowserReportSerializer`; on the first invalid report it logs a warning and immediately returns `Response({...}, status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` (see new loop in `post()`), so it will not process remaining valid reports in the batch. Previously it iterated and always returned 200 (unless construction raised), so this is a concrete response/contract change for batched submissions. Whether this is "wrong" is product/contract-dependent, but it is a real behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:37 — New `owner` ActorField accepted on detector create/update without validating the user/team belongs to the detector's organization, and the detector serializer response is not updated to return it

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` to `BaseDetectorTypeValidator` and explicitly persists it to `Detector.owner_user_id` / `owner_team_id` on both update and create. The claim that org membership isn’t validated is contradicted by new tests in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py` (`test_owner_not_in_organization`) expecting a 400 when the actor is not in the org, implying the validation is already handled (likely by `ActorField` and/or surrounding endpoint validation). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:88 — Endpoint now does a replay Snuba query and nodestore fetch by default with a new undocumented `enable_error_context` query param (opt-out), changing default request behavior/latency with no schema docs

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get now always performs an extra Snuba query (query_replay_instance + process_raw_response) to derive error_ids and, by default, performs a nodestore fetch (fetch_error_details uses nodestore.backend.get_multi) unless the caller sets query param enable_error_context=false (default is treated as true via request.query_params.get(..., "true")). This is a behavior/latency change and the new query param is not reflected in any schema/endpoint docs in the diff (only @extend_schema(tags=["Replays"]) is present). This is a valid review concern but not a clearly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:143 — Merged-PR comment format for GitHub/GitLab changes (culprit subtitle removed, bullet `-` to `*`, title truncated to 50 chars, trailing newline added) altering externally posted comment content

This will change externally posted comment content/format (bullet marker, removed subtitle, added blank lines from joining strings that already end with `\n`), but the diff doesn't show a functional defect—tests were updated to expect the new output—so it's best treated as a non-bug but impactful behavior change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:154 — Error timestamps (seconds from nodestore) are compared against rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds), so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb instead of chronologically interleaved.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, both rrweb/breadcrumb events and fetched error events are treated as comparable numeric timestamps without any indication of differing units. `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[...]["timestamp"]` to `event.get("timestamp", 0)` directly, and the updated test explicitly uses second-based floats for segment events (e.g. 1.5, 2.0) and error events (e.g. 1.0, 3.0), validating correct chronological interleaving. There’s no diff evidence that rrweb timestamps are milliseconds while nodestore timestamps are seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:118 — zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi preserves input order and includes every key; cache-hit reordering or omitted missing keys misattribute event IDs to the wrong error data.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details`, the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. A `get_multi` result is a mapping keyed by node_id; iterating `events.values()` is not guaranteed (by this diff) to be in the same order as `error_ids`, and missing keys could change the length/contents, causing `event_id` to be paired with the wrong `data` (misattribution). The safer approach would index by node_id (or iterate node_ids and look up) rather than zipping against `values()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:52 — Mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, so a report carrying both age=0 and timestamp (or timestamp=0 and age) passes, and reports with neither field are also accepted.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, the mutual-exclusion checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)` in a truthiness context: `validate_timestamp` raises only if `age` is truthy, and `validate_age` raises only if `timestamp` is truthy. This means `age=0` (allowed since `age` has no `min_value`) will not trigger the `timestamp` validator, and `timestamp=0` (explicitly allowed via `min_value=0`) will not trigger the `age` validator—so a payload containing both fields can pass. Also, both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and there is no validator ensuring at least one is present, so reports with neither field are accepted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:104 — fetch_error_details does an unbounded nodestore get_multi over every error_id of the replay (no cap), loading full event payloads just to read title/message/timestamp.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the new `fetch_error_details(project_id, error_ids)` builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(...)]` for every `error_id` and then calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` with no explicit cap/limit. The code then reads fields like `title`, `message`, and `timestamp` from the returned event payloads, implying full event blobs are fetched. This is a concrete, diff-introduced scalability/performance concern (potentially large memory/IO if a replay has many `error_ids`), but not a directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:94 — The Snuba replay query and the full error fetch run on every paginated request, before pagination, and all error events get attached to every page's Seer payload instead of only the ones in that page's time window, so the work and payload size grow with page count.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the endpoint computes `filter_params`, runs `query_replay_instance(...)` and then fetches all `error_events = fetch_error_details(project_id, error_ids)` **before** calling `self.paginate(...)`. Since pagination is client-driven across multiple requests, this extra Snuba replay query + nodestore multi-get will be repeated on every page request. Also, `analyze_recording_segments` is partially applied with the full `error_events` list and `get_request_data(...)` merges those errors with the page’s segment events without filtering errors to the page’s segment time range, so the same full error list can be included in every Seer payload page (and even errors after the last event are appended). This is a concrete perf/payload-size concern introduced by the diff, but not a clear functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:70 — New Snuba query_replay_instance call is unguarded and runs even when enable_error_context=false, so a Snuba failure/timeout now fails the whole breadcrumb summary although error context is optional

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code calls `query_replay_instance(...)` and processes its response to compute `error_ids` *before* checking `enable_error_context` (see the new block that sets `snuba_response`/`response`/`error_ids`, followed by `disable_error_fetching = ...`). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:128 — fetch_error_details zips error_ids with get_multi(...).values() positionally, so any ordering difference in the returned dict silently mislabels error events

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details`, it builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` then calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, but constructs results via `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This assumes `events.values()` is in the same order as the input `node_ids`/`error_ids`, which is not guaranteed by `get_multi` (it returns a dict keyed by node id). If the returned dict insertion/order differs, the code will pair an `event_id` with the wrong event data, mislabeling errors silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:163 — Error event timestamps (seconds from nodestore) are compared with replay breadcrumb timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are all emitted before breadcrumbs and interleaving is wrong

adjudication.rationale: In the new interleaving logic (`gen_request_data`), both sides of the timestamp comparison are treated as plain numeric timestamps with no unit conversion: breadcrumb events use `event.get("timestamp", 0)` from the replay segment JSON, and error events use `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` from nodestore. The accompanying test update explicitly uses second-based float timestamps for both breadcrumbs (e.g., 1.5, 2.0) and errors (e.g., 1.0, 3.0), and verifies correct chronological interleaving. The diff provides no evidence that replay breadcrumb timestamps are milliseconds while nodestore timestamps are seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:121 — fetch_error_details catches all exceptions and silently returns [], hiding nodestore outages behind a degraded summary with no metric

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `fetch_error_details()` which wraps all logic in a broad `except Exception` and, on any failure (including nodestore outages), returns an empty list, causing downstream summarization to proceed without error context (`analyze_recording_segments(..., error_events)`). While it is not completely silent (it calls `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)`), it does intentionally degrade behavior without any explicit metric/counter to surface that error-context fetching failed, which is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/observability concern rather than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:584 — get_environment_info does a per-issue get_recommended_event (Snuba+nodestore) inside the PR-comment task with broad exception swallowing, adding N serial external calls with no timeout budget

The finding’s exact claim that this is definitively "Snuba+nodestore" and has "no timeout budget" isn’t directly proven in the diff, but the per-issue call + broad exception swallowing is clearly introduced and is a valid performance/robustness review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:37 — New detector `owner` ActorField has no validate_owner check that the user/team belongs to the detector's organization, allowing cross-org owner assignment on create/update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:143 — Untrusted event-derived issue title and environment name are interpolated unescaped into markdown link text/backticks in PR bot comments, enabling link/markdown injection in Sentry-authored comments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:104 — New fetch_error_details (nodestore lookup, None filtering, zip alignment of ids to values, exception fallback) and the enable_error_context flag ship with no tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:50 — Serializer age/timestamp mutual-exclusion uses truthiness (age=0 or timestamp=0 slip through) and reports with neither field are accepted, with no tests covering either spec shape or these edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/delayed_workflow.py:652 — get_condition_query_groups/get_groups_to_fire signatures gained a required dcg_to_slow_conditions arg, so existing direct unit-test callers will fail and the new no_slow_condition_groups logging is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates the direct unit-test callers to pass the new required `dcg_to_slow_conditions` argument. In `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_delayed_workflow.py`, `get_condition_query_groups(...)` is now called with `dcg_to_slow_conditions` (computed via `get_slow_conditions_for_groups(...)`), and all `get_groups_to_fire(...)` calls similarly include `self.dcg_to_slow_conditions`. So the claim that “existing direct unit-test callers will fail” is not supported by the diff. While the new `no_slow_condition_groups` logging path in `process_delayed_workflows` is not explicitly asserted in tests here, the finding ties it to failing callers, which is incorrect as shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py:81 — New analytics event is recorded before the feature/permission check with no test asserting when it is (or is not) emitted.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, the diff adds `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` at the start of `post()` (right after the docstring) and only afterwards checks `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)`. This means the analytics event will be emitted even when the feature is disabled and the request is rejected. The diff also adds the event definition/registration (`src/sentry/preprod/analytics.py`) but does not add any tests asserting the event is (or is not) recorded depending on the feature/permission outcome.
